title: File-based task queue with atomic claims and stale takeover
description: This example shows a simple task queue using three directories and atomic file renames. Two agents race to claim a task; the loser can take over if the winner's claim goes stale.

steps.description: The script creates a temporary directory with three subdirectories: inbox, claimed, and done. These hold tasks at each stage.
STALE_AFTER is 300 seconds (5 minutes). A claim older than this is considered abandoned.
post_task writes a task file into the inbox directory.

claim uses os.rename to atomically move a task from inbox to claimed. The rename is atomic on one filesystem, so exactly one agent wins. The loser gets FileNotFoundError and returns False. The winner writes a .claim file with its name and timestamp.
The atomic rename is the whole protocol. No locks needed because the filesystem guarantees the rename either happens completely or not at all.
take_if_stale reads the .claim file, checks if the claim age exceeds STALE_AFTER, and if so, overwrites the claim with the new agent's info and returns True.
finish moves the task from claimed to done, deletes the .claim file, and writes a result file with the finishing agent's name and the result text.
show lists the contents of all three directories so we can see the state.
A task is posted. Agent A claims it (True). Agent B tries to claim it (False). The directories show the task in claimed with its .claim file.

steps.question: What happens when agent B calls take_if_stale after agent A's claim is backdated past STALE_AFTER?
steps.answer: The claim age exceeds STALE_AFTER, so take_if_stale returns True and agent B becomes the new claimant.

steps.description: The script simulates a crash by backdating agent A's claim timestamp by STALE_AFTER + 1 seconds. Then agent B calls take_if_stale and succeeds.
Agent A claims the task. The claim succeeds and the .claim file is written.
Agent B tries to claim the same task. The file is no longer in inbox, so os.rename raises FileNotFoundError and claim returns False.
Agent B calls take_if_stale. The backdated claim is older than STALE_AFTER, so the function returns True and agent B takes over.
Agent B finishes the task. The task moves to done, the .claim file is deleted, and a result file is created with agent B's answer.
